label: adaptive-summary-comparison
note: Illustrative stated starting points; live provider calls, no user Chart writes.

context.intention: I maintain a consistent workout routine.
context.actualStartingPoint: I exercise sporadically. I can use three 30-minute slots each week for bodyweight exercise at home.
context.destinationDescription: I maintain a consistent workout routine.

analysis.startingPointSummary: The person currently exercises sporadically and has three 30-minute home bodyweight slots available each week.
assumptions: Consistency means the routine is repeated from week to week, not a one-off burst.
Bodyweight exercise at home is the main available modality.
No extra equipment, coaching, or additional time is assumed.

routeDesign.complexityReason: This is a habit-building health goal with a clear starting point and limited constraints. The route needs to show distinct state changes: first workable week, repeatability across an off-week, then a self-directed routine that holds without relying on momentum.
routeDesign.countReason: Three waypoints are enough to capture the meaningful changes from sporadic exercise to a consistent routine without adding filler: establish one repeatable week, prove it survives disruption, and then show the routine is being sustained independently.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: The first real change is a full week completed within the available three 30-minute home slots, showing the routine is no longer sporadic.

raw.destination: I maintain a consistent workout routine

waypoints.title: Complete one planned workout week
waypoints.rationale: This shows the routine can happen inside the time and setting already available.
waypoints.completionCriteria: A full week is completed with three planned 30-minute bodyweight workouts at home.

moves.title: Choose three workout days this week
moves.rationale: This turns the available slots into a specific weekly plan.

moves.title: Write a 30-minute bodyweight session outline
moves.rationale: This removes decision-making when it is time to start.

moves.title: Complete all three sessions in the chosen week
moves.rationale: This is the first visible proof that the routine fits real life.

waypoints.title: Repeat the routine through a disrupted week
waypoints.rationale: Consistency becomes meaningful when it holds even if the week is not smooth.
waypoints.completionCriteria: In a later week with a normal disruption, the person still completes the same three planned workouts.

moves.title: Keep the same three weekly workout slots
moves.rationale: Repeating the structure makes the routine easier to return to.

moves.title: Use a shortened version if one session is pressured for time
moves.rationale: This protects the habit from breaking when the week gets messy.

moves.title: Finish the week with all three sessions done
moves.rationale: This shows the routine survives disruption rather than depending on a perfect week.

waypoints.title: Hold a self-directed weekly rhythm
waypoints.rationale: This is the point where the routine is being maintained rather than rebuilt each week.
waypoints.completionCriteria: The person can set up and complete three home workouts in a typical week without needing to restart the routine each time.

moves.title: Start each week by placing the three workouts on the calendar
moves.rationale: This keeps the routine anchored before the week fills up.

moves.title: Adjust one session without losing the others when plans change
moves.rationale: This makes the routine flexible enough to keep going.

moves.title: Keep completing the three-session pattern for several weeks
moves.rationale: This shows the routine is now self-directed and stable.

suggestedOneMove.title: Choose three workout days this week
suggestedOneMove.rationale: It is the smallest concrete start toward the first completed workout week.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Use your three 30-minute home slots to make the routine visible in the week, then prove it still holds when the week is imperfect.

context.intention: I successfully complete my first half marathon.
context.actualStartingPoint: I run 5 km comfortably twice a week. I can train three days each week. I have never completed a half marathon.
context.destinationDescription: I successfully complete my first half marathon.

analysis.startingPointSummary: The person already runs 5 km comfortably twice a week and can train three days per week, but has never completed a half marathon.
assumptions: The destination is the first half marathon finish, not a specific finish time.
Training is limited to three days per week as stated.
No extra coaching, equipment, or injury history is assumed.

routeDesign.complexityReason: This is a first-endurance-event goal with clear dependencies: build a reliable training base, extend long-run durability, make the body ready for race distance, then complete the event.
routeDesign.countReason: Four waypoints cover the distinct achievements without turning the route into a distance ladder: establish a workable longer-week rhythm, extend the long run meaningfully, show readiness to sustain half-marathon effort, and finish the race.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: A first workable change would be a week where the person completes three runs with one longer run beyond their current 5 km comfort zone and recovers normally.

raw.destination: Successfully complete a first half marathon

waypoints.title: Hold a first three-run training week
waypoints.rationale: This shows the routine can support half-marathon training beyond the current twice-weekly pattern.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Complete one week with three runs, including one run longer than the current comfortable 5 km run, without needing to skip the week.

moves.title: Add a third run on a separate day
moves.rationale: Create the first full training week shape within the time available.

moves.title: Make one run slightly longer than 5 km
moves.rationale: Start extending endurance without changing the whole routine at once.

moves.title: Keep the other two runs easy
moves.rationale: Protect recovery so the added run is sustainable.

waypoints.title: Extend the long run beyond easy comfort
waypoints.rationale: A longer weekly run is the main physical bridge from 5 km comfort to half-marathon readiness.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Reach a longest run of 10 km in training and finish it without stopping.

moves.title: Increase the long run by a small step
moves.rationale: Lengthen the weekend run gradually from the current 5 km base.

moves.title: Keep weekly running to three days
moves.rationale: Use the existing schedule rather than adding unsupported volume.

moves.title: Practice an easy pace for the longer run
moves.rationale: Build distance first so the body adapts before speed matters.

waypoints.title: Handle half-marathon distance in training
waypoints.rationale: This confirms the body can manage the event distance before race day.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Complete a training long run at or near half-marathon distance and recover normally within the following days.

moves.title: Lengthen the long run again in controlled steps
moves.rationale: Move from 10 km toward race distance without jumping too far.

moves.title: Keep the rest of the week easy
moves.rationale: Preserve recovery as the distance load rises.

moves.title: Use one full dress rehearsal week
moves.rationale: Test the routine, fueling, and recovery pattern around the longer run.

waypoints.title: Finish the half marathon
waypoints.rationale: The goal is reached only when the race itself is completed.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Cross the finish line of a half marathon.

moves.title: Choose a realistic race day effort plan
moves.rationale: Settle on an easy, finish-focused approach for the event.

moves.title: Taper before race day
moves.rationale: Reduce training load so the body is ready to run the event.

moves.title: Run the race and keep moving to the finish
moves.rationale: Complete the full distance on the day.

suggestedOneMove.title: Add a third run on a separate day
suggestedOneMove.rationale: It is the smallest concrete step toward a workable half-marathon training week.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Keep the focus on endurance and recoverability, not speed; the first signs of progress should be in how far you can run and how well you bounce back.

context.actualStartingPoint: Anchor is launched with 20 paying users. I am the solo developer, with 10 hours a week for growth and no paid advertising budget. I can contact current users and have subscription analytics.

vision.title: A sustainable Anchor business
vision.description: 10,000 paying users who continue using Anchor

analysis.startingPointSummary: Anchor is already launched with 20 paying users. The founder is solo, has 10 hours a week for growth, no paid ad budget, and can contact current users and review subscription analytics.
assumptions: Paying users can be contacted for feedback and usage signals.
Subscription analytics can show cohort, churn, and conversion patterns.
Growth must rely on product, retention, and repeatable low-cost acquisition rather than paid advertising.

routeDesign.complexityReason: This is a multi-stage business growth goal with dependent outcomes: first a stable retention signal, then a repeatable acquisition source, then paid conversion improvements, then operational capacity to support scale, before the final user base target.
routeDesign.countReason: Five waypoints cover the distinct achievements needed from the current base of 20 users to a sustainable 10,000-user business without adding filler: retention proof, first repeatable acquisition channel, improved conversion, scalable operating rhythm, and the final scale milestone.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: The first meaningful change is evidence that the current 20 paying users are staying active long enough to validate the product and reveal retention patterns, not just initial signups.

raw.destination: 10,000 paying users who continue using Anchor

waypoints.title: Show early retention in the current user base
waypoints.rationale: Before scaling, Anchor needs proof that existing paying users continue using it.
waypoints.completionCriteria: At least 12 of the current 20 paying users remain active and paying after 30 days.

moves.title: Review current subscriber activity and churn
moves.rationale: Find who is still using Anchor and where drop-off starts.

moves.title: Contact active and inactive users for short feedback
moves.rationale: Learn what keeps people paying and what causes them to leave.

moves.title: Make one product change that addresses the most common retention issue
moves.rationale: Improve the reason people keep using Anchor.

moves.title: Check the next cohort of users for the same retention pattern
moves.rationale: Confirm the change is affecting repeat use, not just one group.

waypoints.title: Find one repeatable low-cost acquisition source
waypoints.rationale: Growth needs a channel that can produce new users without paid ads.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Anchor has one acquisition source that can repeatedly bring in new paying users at low cost.
requirements: One offer or message that fits that source
At least two repeatable acquisition attempts
New paying users attributed to the source

moves.title: List the places where current users can realistically come from
moves.rationale: Focus on channels that fit a solo founder and no ad budget.

moves.title: Test one outreach or content message in the best-fit channel
moves.rationale: See whether the message draws interest from likely users.

moves.title: Track which messages lead to signups and payments
moves.rationale: Separate promising distribution from noise.

moves.title: Repeat the best-performing approach twice more
moves.rationale: Confirm the channel can be used again, not just once.

waypoints.title: Improve trial to paid conversion
waypoints.rationale: A repeatable source only matters if more of those users become paying users.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Anchor consistently adds 50 new paying users in a month from organic or low-cost acquisition.

moves.title: Tighten the signup and paywall path
moves.rationale: Reduce friction between interest and payment.

moves.title: Use user feedback to sharpen the value message
moves.rationale: Make the paid offer easier to understand.

moves.title: Run one conversion-focused product or copy change at a time
moves.rationale: Learn what improves payment decisions.

moves.title: Measure which change increases paid conversions
moves.rationale: Keep only the changes that move users to payment.

waypoints.title: Operate growth with a repeatable weekly rhythm
waypoints.rationale: Scaling needs a sustainable process the solo founder can maintain.
waypoints.completionCriteria: A weekly growth routine is in place that consistently covers retention, acquisition, and conversion work within 10 hours.
requirements: One acquisition action shipped every week
One product or retention improvement shipped every week

moves.title: Set a fixed weekly review using the analytics you already have
moves.rationale: Use one regular pass to decide what to do next.

moves.title: Reserve one block for user contact each week
moves.rationale: Keep direct feedback flowing from real paying users.

moves.title: Reserve one block for acquisition experiments each week
moves.rationale: Keep new-user input coming through the chosen channel.

moves.title: Reserve one block for product changes each week
moves.rationale: Turn what you learn into shipped improvements.

waypoints.title: Reach 10,000 paying users
waypoints.rationale: This is the final observable scale outcome of retention and repeatable growth.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Anchor reaches 10,000 paying users and the base continues using the product.

moves.title: Keep the best acquisition channel active month after month
moves.rationale: Sustained inflow is needed to reach the target.

moves.title: Keep improving retention from customer feedback and analytics
moves.rationale: Growth only holds if users continue paying.

moves.title: Remove bottlenecks that slow onboarding or payment
moves.rationale: Protect conversion as volume increases.

moves.title: Monitor the user base for churn and channel performance
moves.rationale: Keep the system stable while it scales.

suggestedOneMove.title: Review current subscriber activity and churn
suggestedOneMove.rationale: This is the smallest useful step toward proving retention in the current 20-user base.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Start with retention in the current user base, then use what you learn to build a repeatable low-cost acquisition path.
